claim: ORACLE is a high-throughput, locus-specific, phage genome engineering method that creates large, unbiased libraries of phage variants.
source: Here, we carried out DMS, a high-throughput experimental technique, of the tip domain of the T7 phage RBP (tail fiber) to uncover molecular determinants of activity and host range. The tip domain is the distal region of the tail fiber that makes primary contact with the host receptor (González-García et al., 2015; Molineux, 2001; Qimron et al., 2006). We developed ORACLE (Optimized Recombination, Accumulation, and Library Expression), a high-throughput, locus-specific, phage genome engineering method to create a large, unbiased library of phage variants at a targeted gene locus.
evidence: The manuscript describes the development and application of ORACLE as a new method, supported by experimental data showing its capabilities.

claim: The tip domain of T7 phage tail fiber makes primary contact with the host receptor.
source: The tip domain is the distal region of the tail fiber that makes primary contact with the host receptor (González-García et al., 2015; Molineux, 2001; Qimron et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Using ORACLE, 1660 single amino acid substitution variants of the T7 tip domain were systematically created.
source: Using ORACLE, we systematically and comprehensively mutated the tip domain by making all single amino acid substitutions at every site (1660 variants) and quantified the functional role of all variants on multiple bacterial hosts.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental creation of this specific number of variants.

claim: T7 acceptor phages lacking a wildtype tail fiber gene cannot plaque on E. coli.
source: T7 acceptor phages lacking a wildtype tail fiber gene cannot plaque on E. coli and do not spontaneously reacquire the tail fiber during propagation (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and supplementary figures.

claim: T7 acceptor phages have no plaquing deficiency relative to wildtype when the tail fiber gene is provided from a helper plasmid.
source: Furthermore, the T7 acceptor phages have no plaquing deficiency relative to wildtype when the tail fiber gene is provided from a helper plasmid (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The recombination rate in ORACLE is approximately 7.19×10⁻⁴.
source: (C) Concentration of total (Total T7) and recombined (T7 Rec) phages after a single passage on host containing Cre recombinase system. Recombination rate is estimated to be ~7.19x10-4.
evidence: This is calculated from experimental measurements shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Recombined phages were enriched by over one thousandfold when an optimized gRNA targeting the fixed sequence was used.
source: Recombined phages were highly enriched by over one thousandfold in the phage population when an optimized gRNA targeting the fixed sequence was used, whereas a randomized control gRNA yielded no enrichment of recombined phages (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2E, F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and supplementary figures.

claim: The post-ORACLE phage library retained 99.8% coverage compared to the input donor plasmid library.
source: The post-ORACLE phages were mildly skewed toward more abundant members but remained generally evenly distributed and comparable to the distribution of variants in the input donor plasmid library, retaining 99.8% coverage (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The flexible C-terminal end of the tip domain (residue positions 552–554) broadly tolerates nearly all substitutions across all three hosts.
source: To validate the functional relevance of the screen, we hypothesized that the flexible C-terminal end (residue positions 552–554 and a three-residue extension if the stop codon is substituted) is unlikely to have any structural or host recognition role. As expected, these positions broadly tolerated nearly all substitutions across all three hosts, indicating that the functional scores likely reflect true biological effects (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-E.

claim: T7 variants appeared most adapted to BW25113 and least adapted to 10G based on the fraction of depleted variants.
source: Between the three hosts, T7 variants appeared most and least adapted to BW25113 and 10G, respectively, as evidenced by the fraction of depleted variants (FN < 0.1) after selection on each host (10G: 0.66 ± 0.03; BL21: 0.59 ± 0.01; and BW25113: 0.51 ± 0.01; all significantly different from each other with p<0.05) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Wildtype T7 performed poorly on 10G (F = 0.77 ± 0.05) but significantly better on BL21 (F = 2.92 ± 0.2, p < 0.01) and BW25113 (F = 2.26 ± 0.1, p < 0.01).
source: Furthermore, wildtype T7 fared relatively poorly on 10G (F = 0.77 ± 0.05), indicating a fitness impediment, but performed significantly better on BL21 (F = 2.92 ± 0.2, p < 0.01) and BW25113 (F = 2.26 ± 0.1, p < 0.01) (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements of functional scores.

claim: The best performing variants on 10G were 10 times more enriched than wildtype.
source: In fact, the best performing variants on 10G were 10 times more enriched than wildtype, suggesting substantially higher activity (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: No variant performed exceptionally well on all three hosts (FN > 2).
source: No variant performed exceptionally well on all hosts (FN > 2, Figure 2F); however, 406 variants were tolerated on all three hosts (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: 406 variants were tolerated on all three hosts.
source: No variant performed exceptionally well on all hosts (FN > 2, Figure 2F); however, 406 variants were tolerated on all three hosts (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: On 10G, there was enrichment of larger and more hydrophilic amino acids and depletion of hydrophobic amino acids.
source: On 10G, there was enrichment of larger and more hydrophilic amino acids and depletion of hydrophobic amino acids (all p < 0.001, r > 0.12), which is visually striking on the heatmap (see R, K, and H substitutions in Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: On BW25113, hydrophobic residues were modestly enriched.
source: On BW25113, hydrophobic residues were modestly enriched (all p < 0.034, r > 0.07) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2H), a trend opposite to 10G.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: No significant enrichment or depletion was observed on BL21.
source: In contrast, no significant enrichment or depletion was observed on BL21 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F–H).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Enriched substitutions fall predominantly on four exterior loops (BC, DE, FG, and HI), the adjoining region (β-strand H) close to exterior loop HI, and less frequently on the 'side' of the tip domain.
source: These fall predominantly on four exterior loops (BC, DE, FG, and HI), the adjoining region (β-strand H) close to exterior loop HI, and less frequently on the 'side' of the tip domain.
evidence: This is based on mapping experimental data onto the protein structure.

claim: At positions N501 and R542, only positively charged residues (R, K, and H) were tolerated on 10G and BL21, while many more substitutions were tolerated on BW25113.
source: On 10G and BL21, only positively charged residues (R, K, and H) were tolerated at residues 501 and 542, while in contrast many more substitutions were tolerated at both residues on BW25113.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: R542Q is the best performing variant on BW25113 (FN = 3.31) but is depleted on 10G and BL21.
source: One such substitution, R542Q, is the best performing variant on BW25113 (FN = 3.31) but is conspicuously depleted on 10G and BL21, suggesting that even subtle molecular disparities can lead to large biases in activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental functional scores.

claim: D540 is critical for host recognition on BW25113.
source: We hypothesize that D540 is critical for host recognition on BW25113.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on experimental observations of substitution patterns.

claim: S541D is the third highest scoring substitution on BW25113 (FN = 2.82) while this substitution is depleted on 10G and BL21.
source: This hypothesis is further supported by enrichment of adjacent S541D on BW25113 (FN = 2.82, the third highest scoring substitution), while this substitution is depleted on 10G and BL21 (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental functional scores.

claim: The hydrophobic core comprising W474, I495, W496, I497, Y515, W523, L524, F526, I528, F535, and I548 is essential for stability and highly intolerant to substitutions.
source: The hydrophobic core comprising W474, I495, W496, I497, Y515, W523, L524, F526, I528, F535, and I548 is essential for stability and therefore is highly intolerant to substitutions (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: An elaborate network of salt bridge interactions involving D489, R491, R493, R508, and D512 in the interior loops is intolerant to substitutions.
source: Other intolerant positions include an elaborate network of salt bridge interactions involving D489, R491, R493, R508, and D512 in the interior loops, which likely constrain the orientation of the tip domain relative to the shaft (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on experimental data and structural analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Several glycines (G476, G510, G522, and G532) are highly intolerant to substitutions.
source: Interestingly, several glycines (G476, G510, G522 ,and G532) are highly intolerant to substitutions.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: Functional positions are densely concentrated along exterior loops BC, DE, FG, and HI, as well as adjacent β-sheet residues.
source: We found that functional positions did typically point outward and are densely concentrated along exterior loops BC, DE, FG, and HI, as well as adjacent β-sheet residues.
evidence: This is based on experimental data and structural mapping.

claim: Functional positions were found in β-sheet residues I514, Q527, and K536 located along one side of the tip domain.
source: Functional positions were also found in regions other than exterior loops, such as I514, Q527, and K536, which are β-sheet residues located along one side of the tip domain (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Over 93% of tolerated or functional positions have a substitution that was predicted to be stabilizing by Rosetta.
source: Predicted thermodynamic changes in stability mapped very well with over 93% of tolerated or functional positions having a substitution that was predicted to be stabilizing.
evidence: This is based on computational predictions compared to experimental data.

claim: Gene rfaG transfers glucose to the outer core of LPS and deletion strains lack the outer core of LPS.
source: Gene rfaG (synonyms WaaG or pcsA) transfers glucose to the outer core of LPS and deletion strains lack the outer core of LPS (Pagnout et al., 2019), while rfaD (synonyms gmhD or WaaD) encodes a critical epimerase required for building the inner core of LPS (Valvano et al., 2002; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: rfaD encodes a critical epimerase required for building the inner core of LPS.
source: Gene rfaG (synonyms WaaG or pcsA) transfers glucose to the outer core of LPS and deletion strains lack the outer core of LPS (Pagnout et al., 2019), while rfaD (synonyms gmhD or WaaD) encodes a critical epimerase required for building the inner core of LPS (Valvano et al., 2002; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Deletion of rfaG or rfaD reduces the ability of T7 to infect E. coli by several orders of magnitude.
source: Deletion of either gene reduces the ability of T7 to infect E. coli by several orders of magnitude (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Wildtype T7 has significantly lower functional score on BW25113ΔrfaG (F = 0.09 ± 0.3) and BW25113ΔrfaD (F = 0.03 ± 0.2) compared to BW25113 (F = 2.26 ± 0.1, p < 0.001).
source: This is reflected in the significantly lower functional score of wildtype T7 on BW25113ΔrfaG and BW25113ΔrfaD (F = 0.09 ± 0.3 and F = 0.03 ± 0.2, respectively) in comparison to BW25113 (F = 2.26 ± 0.1, p < 0.001) (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental functional scores.

claim: The number of enriched variants (FN ≥ 2) on BW25113ΔrfaG (55 variants, 3.3%) and BW25113ΔrfaD (68 variants, 4.1%) was over three times higher than BW25113 (16 variants, 1%).
source: The number of enriched variants outperforming wildtype T7 (FN ≥ 2) on the deletion strains (BW25113ΔrfaG: 55 variants, 3.3% and BW25113ΔrfaD: 68 variants, 4.1%) was over three times higher than BW25113 (16 variants, 1%) but comparable to 10G (48 variants, 2.9%) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Top performing variants such as G521H and G521R on BW25113ΔrfaG and S541K and N501H on BW25113ΔrfaD were over 100 times greater than wildtype T7.
source: However, the enrichment scores of top performing variants such as G521H and G521R on BW25113ΔrfaG and S541K and N501H on BW25113ΔrfaD were over 100 times greater than wildtype T7, suggesting strong gain of function on the deletion strains (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Of the 78 variants with FN ≥ 2 on either deletion strain, 45 variants had FN ≥ 2 on both strains.
source: Of the 78 variants with FN ≥ 2 on either deletion strain, 45 variants had FN ≥ 2 on both strains, indicating that variants that performed well on one strain typically performed well on the other strain.
evidence: This is based on experimental data analysis.

claim: Hydrophilic substitutions were more strongly enriched on BW25113ΔrfaG (p < 0.001, r > 0.11) than on BW25113ΔrfaD (p < 0.033, r < 0.10).
source: Nonetheless, hydrophilic substitutions were more strongly enriched on BW25113ΔrfaG (p < 0.001, r > 0.11), but not as significantly on BW25113ΔrfaD (p < 0.033, r < 0.10), suggesting subtle differences in surface chemical properties of deletion strains leading to host-specific enrichments (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D–F).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Most substitutions on deletion strains were concentrated in the exterior loops BG, FG, HI, and β-strand H, all pointing downward toward the bacterial surface.
source: Most substitutions were concentrated in the exterior loops BG, FG, HI, and β-strand H, all pointing downward toward the bacterial surface, reinforcing the functional importance of these regions of the tip domain (Figure 4D, E).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: D540S performed better on BW25113ΔrfaG over wildtype BW25113 by 1–2 orders of magnitude.
source: D540S was particularly noteworthy as it performed better on the deletion strain BW25113ΔrfaG over wildtype BW25113 by 1–2 orders of magnitude.
evidence: This is supported by experimental EOP data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: D540 is critical for infecting wildtype BW25113 likely by interacting with the outer core of LPS.
source: Based on these results, we conclude that D540 is critical for infecting wildtype BW25113 (Figure 3) likely by interacting with the outer core of LPS.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Many truncated variants performed well on BW25113ΔrfaG, including some with FN ≥ 10.
source: Many truncated variants performed well, especially on BW25113ΔrfaG, which included some with FN ≥ 10 (Figure 4—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Variant R525* showed no ability to plaque on any host unless provided the tail fiber in trans.
source: We clonally tested variant R525*, the best performing truncated library member (BW25113ΔrfaG FN = 9.55, BW25113ΔrfaD FN = 75.7), and found that this mutant showed no ability to plaque on any host unless provided the tail fiber in trans.
evidence: This is supported by experimental EOP data.

claim: Acceptor phages altogether lacking a tail fiber were present at extremely low abundance.
source: In fact, acceptor phages altogether lacking a tail fiber were present at extremely low abundance (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental sequencing data.

claim: T7 can infect pathogenic E. coli strain isolate 473 from a UTI patient, but insensitivity arises rapidly.
source: To test this hypothesis, we chose pathogenic E. coli strain isolate 473 isolated from a patient with a UTI (Arthur et al., 1990). Although T7 can infect this UTI strain, insensitivity arises rapidly, a phenomenon all too common with the use of natural phages.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations and citation to the strain source.

claim: Wildtype T7 showed insensitive plaque morphology consisting of small, slow-growing plaques on UTI473.
source: EOP assays for wildtype T7 showed insensitive plaque morphology consisting of small, slow-growing plaques.
evidence: This is based on experimental EOP assays.

claim: No visible lysis was detected after overnight incubation when wildtype T7 was applied to UTI473 in liquid culture (MOI = 1).
source: No visible lysis was detected after overnight incubation when wildtype T7 was applied in liquid culture (MOI = 1), indicating onset of insensitivity.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: The variant library applied on UTI473 cleared the culture (MOI = 1) after overnight incubation.
source: However, the variant library applied on the UTI strain cleared the culture (MOI = 1) after overnight incubation, suggesting that T7 variants are capable of lysing and attenuating insensitivity existing in the pool.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: Variants N501H, D520A, and G521R vastly outperformed wildtype T7 in terms of onset of insensitivity on UTI473.
source: We clonally characterized three variants (N501H, D520A, and G521R) isolated from plaques. All three variants vastly outperformed wildtype T7 in terms of onset of insensitivity.
evidence: This is based on experimental characterization.

claim: Insensitivity emerged approximately 11–13 hr after initial lysis for variants N501H, D520A, and G521R, whereas it took merely 1–2 hr after initial lysis for wildtype T7 on UTI473.
source: Insensitivity emerged approximately 11–13 hr after initial lysis for the three variants, whereas it took merely 1–2 hr after initial lysis for wildtype (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental time course data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: N501H variant lysed UTI473 cells faster and produced a lower bacterial load post lysis compared to wildtype T7.
source: In particular, the N501H variant lysed cells faster and produced a lower bacterial load post lysis, suggesting far greater activity compared to wildtype T7.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 5A.

claim: At all MOIs, wildtype phages lysed UTI473 significantly more slowly compared to N501H phages (all p < 0.05).
source: At all MOIs, wildtype phages lysed UTI473 significantly more slowly compared to N501H phages (all p < 0.05).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: At lower MOI, time to lysis of N501H was half that of wildtype T7 on UTI473.
source: At lower MOI, time to lysis of N501H was half that of wildtype T7, though they were more comparable at higher MOI.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Between MOI of 10⁻¹ and 10⁻⁵, application of N501H phage reduced insensitivity over a 10 hr window, while application of wildtype phages resulted in rapid onset of insensitive bacteria on UTI473.
source: However, between an MOI of 10−1 and 10−5, application of N501H phage reduced insensitivity over a 10 hr window, while application of wildtype phages resulted in rapid onset of insensitive bacteria.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: 118 out of 1660 variants were identified as good candidates for constricting host range (|FD| ≥ 1).
source: We identified 118 out of 1660 variants as good candidates for constricting host range (|FD| ≥ 1, see Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: Of the 118 host-constricting variants, 53 variants favor BW25113 over BL21 and 98 variants favor BW25113 over 10G.
source: Of the 118 variants, 53 variants favor BW25113 over BL21 and 98 variants favor BW25113 over 10G in pairwise comparisons (Figure 6A, C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 6A and C.

claim: Between BL21 and 10G, there are 15 variants that favor BL21 but none that favor 10G.
source: Between BL21 and 10G, there are 15 variants that favor BL21 but none that favor 10G (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is based on analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Variant R542Q showed a significant approximately hundredfold decrease in the ability to plaque on BL21 compared to BW25113.
source: Indeed, R542Q showed a significant approximately hundredfold decrease in the ability to plaque on BL21 compared to BW25113 while 10G plaques were atypically small, indicating a severe growth defect (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental EOP data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Variant D540S showed a significant approximately hundredfold decrease in the ability to plaque on BW25113 compared to BL21 and 10G.
source: In contrast, D540S showed a significant approximately hundredfold decrease in the ability to plaque on BW25113 compared to BL21 and 10G (Figure 6D), confirming the host constriction properties of these variants.
evidence: This is supported by experimental EOP data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Phages constitute unparalleled biological variation found in nature and are called the 'dark matter' of the biosphere.
source: Phages constitute unparalleled biological variation found in nature and are aptly called the 'dark matter' of the biosphere.
evidence: This is a statement drawing from established scientific knowledge.

claim: Fecal viromes estimate 10⁸–10⁹ virus-like particles per gram of feces, but less than a quarter of sequence reads align to existing databases.
source: For instance, fecal viromes estimate 108–109 virus-like particles per gram of feces, but less than a quarter of sequence reads align to existing databases (Reyes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Bacteriophages shape microbial ecosystems by infecting and killing targeted bacterial species.
source: Bacteriophages (or 'phages') shape microbial ecosystems by infecting and killing targeted bacterial species.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Phages are promising tools for treatment of antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections and microbiome manipulation.
source: As a result, they are promising tools for treatment of antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections and microbiome manipulation (Canfield and Duerkop, 2020; Chen et al., 2014; Clokie et al., 2011; Dedrick et al., 2019; Kilcher and Loessner, 2019; Kutter et al., 2015; Mizuno et al., 2020; Sausset et al., 2020; Schooley et al., 2017; Shen et al., 2015; Shkoporov and Hill, 2019; De Sordi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Interaction of phages with their bacterial receptors is a key determinant of their host range and virulence.
source: Interaction of phages with their bacterial receptors is a key determinant of their host range and virulence (Bertozzi Silva et al., 2016; de Jonge et al., 2019; Rousset et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The interaction between phages and bacteria is primarily mediated by the receptor binding proteins (RBPs) of the phage.
source: This interaction is primarily mediated by the receptor binding proteins (RBPs) of the phage (Nobrega et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: RBPs enable phages to adsorb to diverse cell surface molecules, including proteins, polysaccharides, lipopolysaccharides (LPS), and carbohydrate-binding moieties.
source: RBPs enable phages to adsorb to diverse cell surface molecules, including proteins, polysaccharides, lipopolysaccharides (LPS), and carbohydrate-binding moieties.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Phages exhibit high functional plasticity through genetic alterations to RBPs and by natural and laboratory-guided evolution.
source: Phages exhibit high functional plasticity through genetic alterations to RBPs and by natural and laboratory-guided evolution, which can modulate activity and host range to different hosts and environments (Ando et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2017; Dedrick et al., 2019; Dunne et al., 2019; Garcia et al., 2003; Gebhart et al., 2017; Holtzman et al., 2020; Lin et al., 2012; Meyer et al., 2012; Yehl et al., 2019; Yosef et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Survivability of a phage is intimately linked to the adaptability of its RBP.
source: In essence, survivability of a phage is intimately linked to the adaptability of its RBP.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge.

claim: Directed evolution enriches only a small group of 'winners', which makes it difficult to glean a comprehensive mutational landscape of the RBP.
source: Though insightful, directed evolution enriches only a small group of 'winners', which makes it difficult to glean a comprehensive mutational landscape of the RBP (Holtzman et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Random mutagenesis-based screens generate multi-mutant variants whose individual effects cannot be easily deconvolved.
source: Random mutagenesis-based screens generate multi-mutant variants whose individual effects cannot be easily deconvolved (Dunne et al., 2019; Yehl et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Swapping homologous RBPs leads to gain of function; however, the underlying molecular determinants of function can be difficult to explain.
source: Other approaches including swapping homologous RBPs lead to gain of function; however, the underlying molecular determinants of function can be difficult to explain (Ando et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2017; Gebhart et al., 2017; Yosef et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Bacteriophage T7 is a podovirus that infects E. coli.
source: Bacteriophage T7 is a podovirus that infects E. coli.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: T7 has a short non-contractile tail made up of three proteins, including the tail fiber encoded by gp17.
source: T7 has a short non-contractile tail made up of three proteins, including the tail fiber encoded by gp17.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Each of the six tail fibers of T7 is a homotrimer composed of a relatively rigid shaft ending with a β-sandwich tip domain connected by a short loop.
source: Each of the six tail fibers is a homotrimer composed of a relatively rigid shaft ending with a β-sandwich tip domain connected by a short loop (Garcia-Doval and van Raaij, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The tip domain is a major determinant of host range and activity and is often naturally exchanged between phages to readily adapt to new hosts.
source: The tip domain is a major determinant of host range and activity and is often naturally exchanged between phages to readily adapt to new hosts (Fraser et al., 2006; Fraser et al., 2007; Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Single amino acid substitutions to the tip domain are sufficient to alter host range between E. coli strains.
source: Even single amino acid substitutions to this domain are sufficient to alter host range between E. coli strains (Heineman et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The library of tip domain variants spans residue positions 472–554.
source: We generated a library of 1660 single mutation variants of the tip domain, prespecified as chip-based oligonucleotides, where all 19 non-synonymous and 1 nonsense substitution were made at each codon spanning residue positions 472–554 (Figure 2A, residue numbering based on PDB 4A0T).
evidence: This is based on the experimental design described.

claim: Selection on each host gave excellent correlation across biological triplicates.
source: Selection on each host gave excellent correlation across biological triplicates (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Specialization toward a host comes at the cost of sacrificing breadth, mirroring observations made of natural phage populations.
source: Thus, specialization toward a host comes at the cost of sacrificing breadth, mirroring observations made of natural phage populations (Elena et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research and experimental observations.

claim: BL21 has been used to propagate T7 and may have already adapted well to this host over time.
source: This is consistent with our earlier observation that wildtype T7 is generally well adapted to BL21 since it had the fewest variants outperforming wildtype. We reasoned that since BL21 has been used to propagate T7 it may have already adapted well to this host over time.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental observations.

claim: Enrichment patterns suggest directionality to phage–bacterial interactions and orientational bias of the tip domain with respect to the bacterial surface.
source: This suggests directionality to phage–bacterial interactions and orientational bias of the tip domain with respect to the bacterial surface.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data.

claim: Single amino acid substitutions alone can generate broad functional diversity, highlighting the evolutionary adaptability of the RBP.
source: Several key lessons emerged from these host screens. First, single amino acid substitutions alone can generate broad functional diversity, highlighting the evolutionary adaptability of the RBP.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: T7 can be optimized and activity can be increased, even on hosts that T7 is already considered to grow well on.
source: Second, T7 can be optimized and activity can be increased, even on hosts that T7 is already considered to grow well on.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Enrichment patterns on each host follow broad trends but have nuance at each position.
source: Third, enrichment patterns on each host follow broad trends but have nuance at each position.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: There were over 30 residues with contrasting substitution patterns between different hosts.
source: There were over 30 residues with contrasting substitution patterns between different hosts, revealing fascinating features of receptor recognition for T7 (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: N501 and R542 are located on exterior loops oriented away from the phage and toward the receptor.
source: N501 and R542 are located on exterior loops oriented away from the phage and toward the receptor (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: R542 forms a literal 'hook' to interact with the receptor.
source: In fact, R542 forms a literal 'hook' to interact with the receptor (Garcia-Doval and van Raaij, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: D520 or the local region around this exterior loop is more important for receptor recognition in BL21 than it is for the other two hosts.
source: This loop is also oriented downward toward the receptor, and we hypothesize that D520 or the local region around this exterior loop is more important for receptor recognition in BL21 than it is for the other two hosts, mirroring the result for D540 for BW25113.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on experimental observations.

claim: At S519, no substitutions are tolerated in BL21 or 10G but several substitutions are enriched on BW25113.
source: Another stark contrast can be drawn at adjacent S519, where no substitutions are tolerated in BL21 or 10G but several substitutions are enriched on BW25113, indicating that substitutions can improve receptor binding on one host while reducing function on another host.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: G479 may sterically hinder D540 when substituted, resulting in depletion of G479 substitutions on BW25113.
source: Since D540, a receptor-facing position on an exterior loop, is only 6 Å from G479, it is likely that any substitution at G479 may sterically hinder D540, resulting in the noted depletion of G479 substitutions on BW25113.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on structural analysis and experimental data.

claim: Exterior loops and some outward-facing positions in β-sheets act as a reservoir of function-switching and function-enhancing mutations.
source: Overall, these results paint a complex enrichment profile for each host with some broad trends but subtle host-specific effects. These results suggest that exterior loops and some outward-facing positions in β-sheets act as a reservoir of function-switching and function-enhancing mutations, likely promoting host-specific and orientation-dependent interactions between phage and bacterial receptors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: The phage can use the 'side' of the tip domain to engage the receptor, increasing the apparent functional area of the tip domain.
source: This suggests the phage can use the 'side' of the tip domain to engage the receptor, increasing the apparent functional area of the tip domain and highlighting several new regions as valuable engineering targets.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data.

claim: Substitutions predicted to be stable but that are intolerant in the DMS assay may indicate that the substituted residue is necessary for all three hosts.
source: For example, substitutions predicted to be stable but that are intolerant in the DMS assay may indicate that the substituted residue is necessary for all three hosts.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of computational predictions and experimental data.

claim: The tail fiber is considered a reservoir of gain-of-function variants due to its principal role in determining fitness of a phage through host adsorption.
source: The tail fiber is considered a reservoir of gain-of-function variants due to its principal role in determining fitness of a phage through host adsorption (Holtzman et al., 2020; Yehl et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: LPS is a known receptor for T7 in E. coli.
source: To identify a resistant host, we focused on host genes rfaG and rfaD involved in the biosynthesis of surface LPS, which is a known receptor for T7 in E. coli (González-García et al., 2015; Molineux, 2001; Qimron et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Independent replicates showed good correlation for BW25113ΔrfaG (R = 0.99, 0.93, 0.93) but only adequate correlation for BW25113ΔrfaD (R = 0.51, 0.68, 0.39).
source: Independent replicates showed good correlation for BW25113ΔrfaG (R = 0.99, 0.93, 0.93) but only adequate correlation for BW25113ΔrfaD (R = 0.51, 0.68, 0.39) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: The same substitutions were largely enriched in all three replicates on BW25113ΔrfaD, suggesting reproducibility of results.
source: Although the scale of FN was inconsistent across replicates on BW25113ΔrfaD, the same substitutions were largely enriched in all three replicates, suggesting reproducibility of results (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: Fewer infection cycles may be ideal for future work with highly resistant hosts.
source: Separately we examined correlation after selection using only a single infection cycle, which produced more highly correlated results for BW25113ΔrfaD (R = 0.89, 0.90, 0.89) (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), indicating that fewer infection cycles may be ideal for future work with highly resistant hosts.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Enriched variants may have broad affinity for truncated LPS but cannot discriminate based on the length of the LPS.
source: Of the 78 variants with FN ≥ 2 on either deletion strain, 45 variants had FN ≥ 2 on both strains, indicating that variants that performed well on one strain typically performed well on the other strain. This implies that the enriched variants may have broad affinity for truncated LPS but cannot discriminate based on the length of the LPS.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data.

claim: The most enriched variants on deletion strains had large positively charged substitutions (K, R, and H) akin to the enrichment pattern on 10G.
source: Notably, the most enriched variants had large positively charged substitutions (K, R, and H) akin to the enrichment pattern on 10G, suggesting that the bacterial surface of these truncated mutants likely resembles that of 10G.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data.

claim: Results are consistent with a recent continuous evolution study, which identified G480E and G521R as possible gain-of-function variants on a strain similar to BW25113ΔrfaD and G479R and G521S as possible gain-of-function variants on BW25113ΔrfaG.
source: Our results are consistent with a recent continuous evolution study, which identified G480E and G521R as possible gain-of-function variants on a strain similar to BW25113ΔrfaD and G479R and G521S as possible gain-of-function variants on BW25113ΔrfaG (Holtzman et al., 2020), although these variants only represent a small fraction of the gain-of-function variants discovered in our study.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research and comparison to experimental data.

claim: Variants A539R, G521H, and D540S showed significant gain of function on deletion strains based on EOP assays.
source: We validated the results of the pooled selection experiment by clonally testing the ability of phage variants with high FN (A539R, G521H, and D540S) to plaque on the deletion strains based on a standard efficiency of plating (EOP) assay. Indeed, EOP results showed significant gain of function in these variants on the deletion strains (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental EOP data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: When the outer core of the LPS is missing (BW25113ΔrfaG), a substitution at D540 becomes necessary for adsorption either to a different LPS moiety or to an alternative receptor.
source: When the outer core of the LPS is missing (BW25113ΔrfaG), a substitution at this position becomes necessary for adsorption either to a different LPS moiety or to an alternative receptor.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Truncated phages detectable only using deep sequencing may demonstrate how obligate lytic phages could become less active in a bacterial population, slowly replicating alongside their bacterial hosts.
source: These truncated phages, detectable here only using deep sequencing, may demonstrate how obligate lytic phages could become less active in a bacterial population, slowly replicating alongside their bacterial hosts, requiring only a single mutation to become fully active again.
evidence: This is speculation based on experimental observations.

claim: Truncated variants are viable phage variants albeit with a much slower infection cycle, resulting in their inability to form visible plaques.
source: We concluded that these are viable phage variants albeit with a much slower infection cycle, resulting in their inability to form visible plaques.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental observations.

claim: Development of effective phage-based therapeutics is hindered by onset of bacterial resistance, resulting in low phage susceptibility.
source: Despite notable exceptions, in general development of effective phage-based therapeutics is hindered by onset of bacterial resistance, resulting in low phage susceptibility.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Initial application of phages in a laboratory setting may reduce bacterial levels, but the residual bacterial load remains high, causing bacteria to quickly recover after phage application.
source: Although initial application of phages in a laboratory setting may reduce bacterial levels, the residual bacterial load remains high, causing bacteria to quickly recover after phage application (Fister et al., 2016; Huss and Raman, 2020; Silva et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A high ratio of phage to bacteria (MOI) may productively kill bacteria in a laboratory setting by overwhelming a host with many phages.
source: A high ratio of phage to bacteria (multiplicity of infection [MOI]) may productively kill bacteria in a laboratory setting by overwhelming a host with many phages (Abedon, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Ensuring an overwhelming amount of phages in a clinical setting is not always feasible.
source: However, ensuring an overwhelming amount of phages in a clinical setting is not always feasible (Principi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: At high MOI wildtype T7 overwhelms the host before insensitivity arises, while at lower MOI insensitivity can emerge and only variants adapted to the host can effectively kill the host.
source: We postulate that at high MOI wildtype T7 simply overwhelms the host before insensitivity arises, while at lower MOI insensitivity can emerge and only variants adapted to the host can effectively kill the host.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on experimental observations.

claim: ORACLE can generate phage variants superior to wildtype phage that could become starting points for further engineering therapeutic phages.
source: These results indicate that ORACLE can generate phage variants superior to wildtype phage that could then become starting points for further engineering therapeutic phages.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Most phages are specialists that selectively target a narrow range of hosts but are unable to productively infect other closely related hosts.
source: Most phages are specialists that selectively target a narrow range of hosts but are unable to productively infect other closely related hosts (Hyman and Abedon, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Two substitutions, D520Q and V544A, were reported to have a preference for BW25113 and BL21, respectively, in head-to-head comparisons.
source: To check if this FD-based approach is suitable for assessing host specificity, we compared our results with previously published data. Two substitutions, D520Q and V544A, that were reported to have a preference for BW25113 and BL21, respectively, in head-to-head comparisons (Heineman et al., 2008) were placed correctly in our plots, confirming the validity of our FD-based classification scheme.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research and comparison to experimental data.

claim: It would be easier to find a variant capable of specifically lysing BW25113, less so for BL21, and most challenging for 10G.
source: Taken together, our data suggests that it would be easier to find a variant capable of specifically lysing BW25113, less so for BL21, and most challenging for 10G.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Variant R542Q had a greater preference for BW25113 than BL21 or 10G (BW25113 FD = 2.0, BL21 FD = 0, 10G FD = 0).
source: To validate our analysis, we clonally tested variant R542Q, which had a greater preference for BW25113 than BL21 or 10G (BW25113 FD = 2.0, BL21 FD = 0, 10G FD = 0), and variant D540S, which had a greater preference for BL21 and 10G than BW25113 (10G FD = 1.03, BL21 FD = 0.62, BW25113 FD = 0.03).
evidence: This is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: Variant D540S had a greater preference for BL21 and 10G than BW25113 (10G FD = 1.03, BL21 FD = 0.62, BW25113 FD = 0.03).
source: To validate our analysis, we clonally tested variant R542Q, which had a greater preference for BW25113 than BL21 or 10G (BW25113 FD = 2.0, BL21 FD = 0, 10G FD = 0), and variant D540S, which had a greater preference for BL21 and 10G than BW25113 (10G FD = 1.03, BL21 FD = 0.62, BW25113 FD = 0.03).
evidence: This is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: 10G plaques of R542Q were atypically small, indicating a severe growth defect.
source: Indeed, R542Q showed a significant approximately hundredfold decrease in the ability to plaque on BL21 compared to BW25113 while 10G plaques were atypically small, indicating a severe growth defect (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental EOP data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Pairwise comparison is a powerful tool to map substitutions that constrict host range and can be leveraged to tailor engineered phages for targeted hosts.
source: In summary, pairwise comparison is a powerful tool to map substitutions that constrict host range and can be leveraged to tailor engineered phages for targeted hosts.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Cross-comparison between different hosts and selection on resistant hosts allowed mapping of key substitutions leading to host discrimination and gain of function.
source: Cross-comparison between different hosts and selection on resistant hosts allowed us to map key substitutions, leading to host discrimination and gain of function.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Single amino acid substitutions are sufficient to enhance activity and host range, including some that confer dramatic increases in activity or specificity.
source: Single amino acid substitutions are sufficient to enhance activity and host range, including some that confer dramatic increases in activity or specificity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: The functional landscape on each host is unique, reflecting both different molecular preferences of adsorption and the fitness of wildtype T7 on these hosts.
source: The functional landscape on each host is unique, reflecting both different molecular preferences of adsorption and the fitness of wildtype T7 on these hosts.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Substitutions on 10G mirrored substitutions that recovered function on BW25113 mutants with truncated LPS, which shows convergence of selection.
source: Notably, substitutions on 10G (an E. coli K-12 derivative lacking LPS components) mirrored substitutions that recovered function on BW25113 mutants with truncated LPS, which shows convergence of selection.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Function-enhancing substitutions were densely concentrated in the exterior loops, indicating an orientational preference for receptor recognition.
source: Function-enhancing substitutions were densely concentrated in the exterior loops, indicating an orientational preference for receptor recognition.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Function-enhancing substitutions were also found on other surface residues, albeit less frequently, suggesting alternative binding modes of the tip domain for host recognition.
source: However, they were also found on other surface residues, albeit less frequently, suggesting alternative binding modes of the tip domain for host recognition, and several intolerant residues were located in exterior loops.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Several intolerant residues were located in exterior loops.
source: However, they were also found on other surface residues, albeit less frequently, suggesting alternative binding modes of the tip domain for host recognition, and several intolerant residues were located in exterior loops.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: Comparison of functional profiles precisely reveals the regions that are ideal engineering targets for customizing host range and activity.
source: Comparison of these functional profiles precisely reveals the regions that are ideal engineering targets for customizing host range and activity and identifies intolerant residues that should be avoided when engineering synthetic phages.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data.

claim: Deep sequencing can detect and resolve small functional effects over traditional low-throughput plaque assays.
source: These results also highlight the power of deep sequencing to detect and resolve small functional effects over traditional low-throughput plaque assays.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental observations.

claim: Truncation of the tip domain may misorient the phage relative to the receptor, likely resulting in slower growth and deficiency in plaquing, while still capable of replicating.
source: Truncation of the tip domain may misorient the phage relative to the receptor, likely resulting in slower growth and deficiency in plaquing, while still capable of replicating.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on experimental observations.

claim: Inability to plaque may not imply a functionally incompetent phage.
source: Since plaque formation is a complex process, inability to plaque may not imply a functionally incompetent phage.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental observations.

claim: ORACLE is designed as a foundational technology to elucidate sequence–function relationships in phage genes.
source: ORACLE is designed as a foundational technology to elucidate sequence–function relationships in phage genes.
evidence: This is a statement of the purpose of the technology.

claim: On T7, ORACLE can be used to investigate the function of several important genes, including the remainder of the tail fiber and tail structure, capsid components, or lysins and holins.
source: On T7, ORACLE can be used to investigate the function of several important genes, including the remainder of the tail fiber and tail structure, capsid components, or lysins and holins.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications of the technology.

claim: Once the phage variants are created, scaling up ORACLE to investigate potentially tens of hosts merely scales up sequencing volume, not experimental complexity.
source: Once the phage variants are created, scaling up ORACLE to investigate potentially tens of hosts merely scales up sequencing volume, not experimental complexity.
evidence: This is a statement about the scalability of the method.

claim: Any phage with a sequenced genome and a transformable host capable of maintaining a plasmid library should be amenable to ORACLE.
source: Any phage with a sequenced genome and a transformable host capable of maintaining a plasmid library should be amenable to ORACLE because the phage variants are created during the natural infection cycle.
evidence: This is a statement about the generalizability of the method.

claim: ORACLE can be leveraged to tune activity for known phages with high activity or to identify engineering targets that dramatically increase activity for newly isolated natural phages.
source: This approach can be leveraged to tune activity for known phages with high activity, such as T7, or to identify engineering targets that dramatically increase activity for newly isolated natural phages.
evidence: This is speculation about applications of the technology.

claim: Phages constitute the most abundant life form on earth.
source: ORACLE provides a generalized framework to describe sequence–function relationships in phages to elucidate the molecular basis of phages, the most abundant life form on earth.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Less than a quarter of sequence reads from fecal viromes align to existing databases.
source: For instance, fecal viromes estimate 108–109 virus-like particles per gram of feces, but less than a quarter of sequence reads align to existing databases (Reyes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: ORACLE is envisioned as a powerful tool to discover new phage 'parts' from metagenomic sequences.
source: By enabling sequence programmability, we envision ORACLE as a powerful tool to discover new phage 'parts' from metagenomic sequences.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications of the technology.
